question: Evidence gathered supports a bounded from-zero decision. Regional trajectory evidence for F_b011_s030__NC (historical_steer_not_current_guidance, domain [0.0,0.5]) shows the ancestor field moving in signed_dy_A (net_rate 1.714) and signed_dz_A (net_rate -0.761) with spatial_mass net_rate 0.075, while the contrast field is much flatter (signed_dy_A net_rate 0.283, signed_dz_A net_rate -0.410, spatial_mass net_rate 0.0069); these are descriptive complete-window curves, not independent repetitions and not spatial reward gradients. Indexed history for F_b011_s030__reference shows the NC region was never the from-zero region in the historical campaign (all historical rounds used the 20-slot reference region), and the current campaign's only from-zero NC test (R03) gave U_tau 0.0, best_qualified_pic50 8.1278, mean_all_pic50 7.6626, final attainment 0.4167, mean_error 0.4377, native_element_fraction 0.9444, while the from-zero G17 test (R04) was rolled back with final attainment 0.0 and mean_error 0.8622. The suffix NC test (R02) reached final attainment 0.3333 with mean_error 0.0029 and native_element_fraction 0.8889, so formation/retention of the NC layout is not the same question as terminal affinity gain. The prior rollback R04 and the historical R04/R07/R09/R14/R16/R18 rollbacks indicate prior coordinate guidance did not realize the intended N/C layout, consistent with a formation-vs-retention gap rather than a pure under-dose explanation. This is sufficient to select one principal from-zero intervention on the NC region versus the reference region as the discriminating next experiment; no further tool round is required within the budget.
